Independent of the choice of the two terminals

explanation:
The potential difference between point X and Y is given by

VXY = VX VY

= V0 sin(t) V0 sin(t + )

= 2V0 cos(t + ) sin ()

= V0 cos(t + ) = V0 sin (t ).

Similarly, the potential difference between point Y and Z is

VYZ = VY VZ

= V0 sin(t + ) V0 sin(t + )

= 2V0 cos(t + ) sin ()

= V0 cos(t) = V0 sin(t + ),

and the potential difference between point Z and X is

VZX = VZ VX

= V0 sin(t + ) V0 sin(t)

= V0 cos( + ) = V0 sin(t + ).

The rms value of the potential V = V0 sin(t + ) is given by Vrms = V0 / . Thus, rms values of the potentials are . Hence, the reading of the voltmeter is independent of the two terminal i.e., reading is same whether it is connected across X-Y or Y-Z or Z-X.
